Aug, 1998  No.132   Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 J. Littlemore........03    04

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: J. Littlemore, FLINTSHIRE


Dear Ron,

You mentioned a program that
will make a copy of a +3 3.5"
OUTLET on to a 3" automatically.
How do I get a copy?

          Yours Sincerely,

            J. Littlemore


Brian Cavers to J. Littlemore



There are two programs. One is
OUT3TO35 which converts the nor-
mal OUTLET 3" disk to 3.5" and
OUT35TO3 which converts the 3.5"
version back to 3". It will only
convert back ones created by the
OUT3TO35 program because a data
file is stored in User Area 1 on
the 3.5" disk containing info on
which files go on Side A of the
3" disk and which go on Side B.
We create the 3.5" version of
OUTLET ourselves using this pro-
gram so OUT35TO3 should work on
them.

Both programs are in this issue.


It must be remembered that any
copies made are only for use by
the reader doing it. Copies of
OUTLET must not be sold or given
to others and any copies must be
destroyed if one sells or gives
away the original.

We don't mind a single copy be-
ing passed to a friend as a one
off as a genuine sample or demo
of what OUTLET is about.

                      Brian

From: Vic Bishop, LANCS..

Dear Brian,

Regarding your reply to my lett-
er in last month's OUTLET, the
command...

POKE @6,1 (+3 FORMAT LPRINT "u")
RESTORE

          ...is not accepted [by
the BASIC editor]. The cursor
appears after '6,1'. I could get
no further.  Yes, the printer
does accept Epson codes.

                     Vic

Brian Cavers to Vic Bishop

Perhaps I did not make the foll-
owing clear...

POKE @6,1 (+3 FORMAT LPRINT "u")
RESTORE

POKE @6,1 is the command to tell
the Disciple or Plus D to accept
printer control codes.

(+3 FORMAT LPRINT "u") is the
command to tell the Plus 3 to
accept printer control codes and
is purely an alternative for any
users who have a +3.

RESTORE is on a separate line or
if at the end of the previous
line then it must be separated
by a colon.

So, Disciple or Plus D users can
do...

10 POKE @6,1
20 RESTORE
          or...

10 POKE @6,1 : RESTORE

Whereas Plus 3 users can use...

10 FORMAT LPRINT "u"
20 RESTORE

          or...

10 FORMAT LPRINT "u" : RESTORE

Hope that clarifies it. Let me
know if it works, OK.
                        Brian

From: L.G. Baumann

Dear Mr. Cavers,


OPEN #2,"p"
-----------

This is not often seen used. It
diverts the print stream from
the screen to the printer.

In Outlet No. 125 there was a
very good and concise calendar
program.

I do not want to interfere with
other people's programs but per-
haps the author (name not given)
would permit me to use this as
an example.


There is a statement that for a
printout one should change all
the PRINT instructions to LPRINT
- here is a case where the div-
ersion of the stream can be use-
ful.

Insert into the program:

  85 REM OPEN #2,"p"
 185 OPEN #2,"s"

For a printout just remove
temporarily the REM in Line 85
to activate it. Line 185 need
not be disturbed at any time.

Perhaps this would be a useful
place to recall the book tells
us that a CAT can be printed out
with CAT #3,1 or CAT #3,1!
                   L.G. Baumann

From: Miles Kinloch
   Well, you're not going to be-
lieve this, but yet another bug
has surfaced in Betados! It
concerns the short CAT when
there isn't enough memory for
the fast, alphabetically-sorted
variety, and it reverts to the
standard G+DOS routine in +D
ROM. This is fine, except for a
small point that Andy Wright
appears to have overlooked...

It centres around Betados system
variable 124, which holds the
number of tracks in the catalog-
ue. This is checked before the
short CAT takes place but unfor-
tunately it doesn't update the
variable first;it takes the val-
ue already there, left over from
the last operation.

Therefore, if the disk last used
(it could be on either drive)had
a SMALLER directory,the DOS will
base the required workspace on
this and may attempt to execute
the fast CAT when there isn't
enough room... If you're lucky,
this will cause a sector error;
if you're less lucky, a crash.

Sometimes it can happen the oth-
er way round, with less drastic
consequences.If the disk you CAT
first is the one with the LARGER
directory, a high value is then
left in 124 causing the DOS pos-
sibly to overestimate the work-
space needed to fast CAT a norm-
al disk. It may then do a G+DOS
style CAT when it doesn't actu-
ally need to.


Anyway, having diagnosed the bug
and worked out a cure,I was fac-
ed with a problem of finding 12
bytes for the necessary patch.
Well, I had to be ruthless and
raid the SAVE...TO... "Insert
ORIG disc"and "Insert DEST disc"
messages, which I'd already
shortened previously to accommo-
date the essential SNAPFIX!


Instead of two separate mess-
ages, now there's only one:
"CHANGE disc" - just like the
Disciple.


I'm speaking, of course, as a
two-drive user, but I thought
perhaps the original Source and


Target messages are less useful
in Betados anyway, since the
"LOADING..." and "SAVING..."
messages act as a reminder of
which disk to insert next. At
least, I hope that's how single-
drive users will see it!


The discovery of this bug and
the search for the extra RAM may
actually have been a blessing in
disguise for by shortening these
messages, I gained enough space
not only to correct the symptom,
but also to implement OPEN-3-OUT
-something I've always wanted to
put into Betados, but until now
could see no possibility of do-
ing as it needs 31 bytes.


Even so, it was still a tight
squeeze, with only 2 bytes to
spare... Let's just hope there
won't be any more bugs!


The inclusion of OPEN-3-OUT is,
at least in my own opinion, an
important upgrade for Betados,
as it not only lets certain pro-
grams direct their printer out-
put to a file, but also allows
utilities like OUT TO T (+D ver-
sion) to work.

I named the new program BETAFIX2
and have added the Betados vers-
ion of SNAPFIX to it as well,
which simplifies things by hav-
ing everything together in one
program.


Another effect of the bug, is
that if it does branch to do the
G+DOS CAT, it bypasses the
routine to update sys. var. 124,
leaving its value unchanged
afterwards. This is now fixed
too.
          Best wishes,

                Miles



   [ BETAFIX 2 can be found on
   this OUTLET disc - with a
   wealth of information about
   it in the info file...
   "BETAFIX 2 INFO".  -  Ed  ]


From: Peter Angus, SWANSEA





Dear Ron,

You may remember that I wrote to
you recently [OUTLETTERS 130]
because my Plus D and/or inter-
face had stopped working, and I
asked whether you knew of anyone
who could check/repair them.

You weren't able to help in that
respect but did help in a round-
about way.You suggested checking
the small ads in various mags,
and I found three in PC Mart ab-
out Speccy's and related items.


One of these had a Plus D set-up
he was using but willing to sell
but said that he knew quite a
few people with Plus Ds and none
had had any problems with them,
and that as the Plus Ds seemed
to be very reliable, maybe the
fault was elsewhere.He suggested
that before I bought anything I
should check the NMI line. This
was gobbledygook to me but when
he explained further it seemed
worth doing.

I went along to my small local
computer repair firm, told them
what this guy had suggested and
asked if they could help.

They checked it out, found it
wasn't the NMI line at fault but
the Z80 chip.

They changed the chip and in do-
ing so fitted it as a "plug-in"
rather than "soldered-in", so
that if it needed replacing in
the future it would be a simpler
and cheaper job. For `25 all is
now well again.

Change of subject:-

Could you please explain how to
use the "FILE-CHANGE" program in
OUTLET 82, for example,to change
Tasword 2 text files (like this)
to PC.

        Yours sincerely,

          Peter Angus



Ron Cavers to Peter Angus

Glad to hear that your Plus D is
now working OK.

The FILE-CHANGE program in Issue
NO.82 of OUTLET is only intended
to change to other file formats
on the Spectrum. You can convert
text files(and even BASIC progr-
ams) over to the PC but you need
the Spectrum Z80(Lunter)emulator
and one of our PD programs to do
it.

If you have access to a PC and
the emulator then let me know
and I'll send you details though
we'll probably publish details
in the August issue of OUTLET
anyway (see next page - Brian)
                            Ron

Brian Cavers to Peter Angus

I wrote a PC program yonks ago
that converts a Lunter emulator
TAP file to a normal PC file. It
is called TAP2ASCI.EXE but it
does not seem to have appeared
in the PC OUTLET. I was rather
surprised at this but then I
remembered that I had sent Brian
Gaff a copy to include with the
emulator (after all, it is of no
use without the emulator).

With the registered copy of the
emulator comes a program that
can transfer files straight off
a +D disk in the PC drive into a
PC TAP file. This can be loaded
into the emulator as a pseudo
tape file. My program converts
it to a normal PC text file.

If you don't have this with the
emulator, or indeed,if any other
OUTLET reader would like a copy
then I can arrange to put it in
a future issue of OUTLET.

However,if you have the emulator
but not TAP2ASCI.EXE then you
can still convert +D text files
by loading them into say,TASWORD
2 running in the emulator and
then using the option to save a
block of memory to a PC file. If
anyone wants full details of
this then let me know.

                       Brian

From:    Ms B.Dowsland
        26 Elsie Street

Dear Outlet Readers,


I may have appealed for these

Longman's O'level Revision.

Scisoft Educational Software

Computer studies (also French

Any Letts Keyword Revision

+3 version of The Last Word




Now for some games:

Jaws 128k the full price version
(two copies of the Alternative
Software budget release have
failed to load in the same place
in the final few loading blocks
obviously a duplication error -
on the other hand I'll accept

lutely sure that your 128 vers-
ion loads)


I really would like Sim City the
+3 Disk version.


I'm still looking for Hungry
Horace, Tranz Am and Backgammon
and Forth on Interface 2 Rom


Now a request for help in gett-
ing through Level 1 of Simpsons
Vs The Space Mutants, I've got
about 15 out of the 20 goals
needed but can't get the last
five. How do I make use of the
rockets, cherry bombs, magnet
and whistle? I used the wrench
on the fire hydrant. It painted
the shop awning red but I didn't
score a point for that.I can use
the rockets and cherry bombs OK
but what do I use them on? I've
found the shortcut using the key
but can't use whistle or magnet.
If we can get to Level 2 Miles
Kinloch will try to put the game
on +D disk. The problems left
to solve are parrot in the cage,
litter on the statue, purple
windows in retirement home and
purple cinema poster.

Lastly, advice to the Outlet 131
reader [J. Cameron] about the
mouse on +3. You're using an art
package that was never designed
for the +3.If you get The Artist
you'll find the mouse works O.K.
For further advice write to me.

Hope I haven't bored anyone but
you did say Ron you was short of
letters of late.

                  Bernadette

P.S. Little known facts: the +2,
+2A, and +3 all transmit the
BRIGHT signal to an Amstrad CPC
colour monitor but not the 128
Sinclair model.
      [I knew that. - Ed]

Brian Cavers>Bernadette Dowsland

Thanks, Bernadette. You might
also try putting a free advert
into MicroMart. You get so many
words free but you can split
each item up into a separate
advert and carefully word it to
use the minimum. You might also
consider a longer lasting advert
in our OUTVERTS or as separate
short ones in OUTBOARD.

                        Brian

From: Gerry Bates

Email:
<gerry@springhill.force9.co.uk>



I was intrigued by Malcolm Perr-
y's item in Outlet 51,"Spreading
the Muck". However, Malcolm - or
more probably his informant -
was a little confused regarding
the operation of the GPS (Global
Positioning System) satellites.
They are not "fixed in space re-
lative to earth and relative to
each other" and the accuracy is
not "1km".

If the satellites were fixed in
space relative to earth they


would have to be in geostation-
ary orbit and would therefore be
above the equator in a straight
line. This would make triangul-
ation ambiguous, as any position
could be north or south of the
equator, and accuracy would det-
eriorate the further north - or
south! -you went. Eventually the
satellites would be invisible.
Height accuracy would also be
very poor.

In fact the 20 or so satellites
- known as the constellation -
are in orbits which are defin-
itely not fixed and are designed
to provide 4 visible satellites
at any one moment, at any point
on the earth's surface, for most
of the time. Four satellites


provide a three dimensional fix
whereas if you're on the ground
you can usually assume your
height and make do with a two
dimensional fix, requiring only
three satellites.

How is the fix calculated? Well,
each satellite is repeatedly
broadcasting a data stream which
includes its position and the
time the data was transmitted.
If it had its own high precision
atomic clock a GPS receiver
could calculate its distance
from the satellite by determin-
ing the transit time of the
signal (at the speed of light).
As you can imagine, this would
make for a very expensive rec-
eiver and certainly not one you
could fit in your pocket!

So, you have a position for the
satellite and the time when it
was at that position, giving the
following equation:
      d = ( Tr - Ts ) x c
where d is the distance from the
receiver to the satellite,Tr and
Ts are the receiver and satell-
ite times and c is the speed of
light. Tr is unknown so d can't
be calculated.

However, simultaneous data from
4 satellites gives enough infor-
mation to calculate the receiver
time and hence a three dimens-
ional fix. (Put simply, thinking
back to your school maths, four
simultaneous equations with four
unknowns can be solved).Assuming
a height makes it possible to
get a fix from 3 satellites.

Accuracy can be as good as 20
to 30 metres from the standard
service but the information
broadcast by the satellites is
deliberately degraded by the US
government to make it useless
for military purposes, reducing
the accuracy to round 100
metres. This is referred to as
Selective Availability or SE.
The imposed error changes conti-
nuously.


A high accuracy, encrypted serv-
ice is available only to the US
military. Ironically, during the
Gulf War the only receivers
available were for the standard
service so SE was turned off!


By using a fixed receiver(within
a 100 miles or so of your own
receiver and therefore receiving
data from the same group of
satellites - this is important)
whose position is accurately
known, it is possible to calcul-
ate, from the known position and
that given by the GPS system,the
error due to SE. Certain other
errors caused by distortion to
the signal path in the upper
atmosphere are also compensated
for.

If this information is passed to
the mobile receiver its own
position can be error corrected
and accuracy improved to 1 to 3
metres. This system is known as
differential GPS or dGPS.


The dGPS corrections broadcast
on the BBC data channels (encr-
ypted) have to be paid for by
annual fee with a choice of acc-
uracy determining the level of
that fee, as Malcolm mentioned.

My own connection with GPS was
to determine the position of a
train which was automatically
recording track data as it trav-
elled round the country. The re-
corded data could be downloaded
for analysis by cellular teleph-
one. Other commercial uses are
by fish ing boats to enable them
to locate nets, etc.

I hope this information is use-
ful.
                  Gerry Bates.

Brian Cavers to Gerry Bates

Yes - and nice and clear. You
ought to write Microsoft's on-
line help then it might be more
useful. I especially like that
part about having a fixed recei-
ver whose position is precisely
known so one can caculate the
deliberate errors! It seems obv-
ious when you know how. It is
surprising that the USA bothers
to keep on reducing the accuracy
though if it can be got round so
relatively easily.


                         Brian.

I was intrigued by Malcolm Perr- y's item in Outlet 51,"Spreading the Muck". However, Malcolm - or more probably his informant - was a little confused regarding the operation of the GPS (Global Positioning System) satellites. They are not "fixed in space re- lative to earth and relative to each other" and the accuracy is not "1km".

If the satellites were fixed in space relative to earth they

would have to be in geostation- ary orbit and would therefore be above the equator in a straight line. This would make triangul- ation ambiguous, as any position could be north or south of the equator, and accuracy would det- eriorate the further north - or south! -you went. Eventually the satellites would be invisible. Height accuracy would also be very poor.

In fact the 20 or so satellites - known as the constellation - are in orbits which are defin- itely not fixed and are designed to provide 4 visible satellites at any one moment, at any point on the earth's surface, for most of the time. Four satellites

provide a three dimensional fix whereas if you're on the ground you can usually assume your height and make do with a two dimensional fix, requiring only three satellites.

How is the fix calculated? Well, each satellite is repeatedly broadcasting a data stream which includes its position and the time the data was transmitted. If it had its own high precision atomic clock a GPS receiver could calculate its distance from the satellite by determin- ing the transit time of the signal (at the speed of light). As you can imagine, this would make for a very expensive rec- eiver and certainly not one you could fit in your pocket!

So, you have a position for the satellite and the time when it was at that position, giving the following equation: d = ( Tr - Ts ) x c where d is the distance from the receiver to the satellite,Tr and Ts are the receiver and satell- ite times and c is the speed of light. Tr is unknown so d can't be calculated.

However, simultaneous data from 4 satellites gives enough infor- mation to calculate the receiver time and hence a three dimens- ional fix. (Put simply, thinking back to your school maths, four simultaneous equations with four unknowns can be solved).Assuming a height makes it possible to get a fix from 3 satellites.

Accuracy can be as good as 20 to 30 metres from the standard service but the information broadcast by the satellites is deliberately degraded by the US government to make it useless for military purposes, reducing the accuracy to round 100 metres. This is referred to as Selective Availability or SE. The imposed error changes conti- nuously.

A high accuracy, encrypted serv- ice is available only to the US military. Ironically, during the Gulf War the only receivers available were for the standard service so SE was turned off!

By using a fixed receiver(within a 100 miles or so of your own receiver and therefore receiving data from the same group of satellites - this is important) whose position is accurately known, it is possible to calcul- ate, from the known position and that given by the GPS system,the error due to SE. Certain other errors caused by distortion to the signal path in the upper atmosphere are also compensated for.

If this information is passed to the mobile receiver its own position can be error corrected and accuracy improved to 1 to 3 metres. This system is known as differential GPS or dGPS.

The dGPS corrections broadcast on the BBC data channels (encr- ypted) have to be paid for by annual fee with a choice of acc- uracy determining the level of that fee, as Malcolm mentioned.

My own connection with GPS was to determine the position of a train which was automatically recording track data as it trav- elled round the country. The re- corded data could be downloaded for analysis by cellular teleph- one. Other commercial uses are by fish ing boats to enable them to locate nets, etc.

I hope this information is use- ful. Gerry Bates.

Brian Cavers to Gerry Bates

Yes - and nice and clear. You ought to write Microsoft's on- line help then it might be more useful. I especially like that part about having a fixed recei- ver whose position is precisely known so one can caculate the deliberate errors! It seems obv- ious when you know how. It is surprising that the USA bothers to keep on reducing the accuracy though if it can be got round so relatively easily.

**Brian Cavers отвечает Vic Bishop:**

Возможно, я не совсем ясно выразился...

```basic
POKE @6,1 (+3 FORMAT LPRINT "u")
RESTORE
```

`POKE @6,1` — это команда, сообщающая Disciple или Plus D, что нужно принимать управляющие коды принтера.

`(+3 FORMAT LPRINT "u")` — это команда для Plus 3, предписывающая принимать управляющие коды принтера, и это всего лишь альтернатива для тех пользователей, у кого +3.

`RESTORE` пишется на отдельной строке, либо, если в конце предыдущей строки, то должна отделяться двоеточием.

Таким образом, пользователи Disciple или Plus D могут сделать так:

```basic
10 POKE @6,1
20 RESTORE
```
или...
```basic
10 POKE @6,1 : RESTORE
```

В то время как пользователи Plus 3 могут использовать:

```basic
10 FORMAT LPRINT "u"
20 RESTORE
```
или...
```basic
10 FORMAT LPRINT "u" : RESTORE
```

Надеюсь, теперь всё понятно. Дайте знать, сработает ли.

Brian

**От: Miles Kinloch**

Что ж, вы не поверите, но в Betados всплыл еще один баг! Он касается короткого каталога (short CAT), когда не хватает памяти для быстрой версии с алфавитной сортировкой, и система возвращается к стандартной процедуре G+DOS в ПЗУ +D. Все бы ничего, если бы не одна мелкая деталь, которую Andy Wright, судя по всему, упустил из виду...

Все дело в системной переменной Betados 124, которая хранит количество дорожек в каталоге. Она проверяется перед выполнением короткого CAT, но, к сожалению, переменная предварительно не обновляется; берется значение, уже находящееся там, оставшееся от последней операции.

Поэтому, если на последнем использованном диске (он мог быть в любом дисководе) каталог был МЕНЬШЕГО размера, DOS выделит необходимую рабочую область на основе этих данных и может попытаться выполнить быстрый CAT, когда места на самом деле недостаточно... Если вам повезет, это приведет к ошибке сектора; если повезет меньше — к зависанию.

Иногда это может происходить и в обратную сторону, с менее фатальными последствиями. Если первый диск, на котором вы сделали CAT, имел БОЛЬШИЙ каталог, то в 124 останется высокое значение, из-за чего DOS, возможно, переоценит размер рабочей области, необходимой для быстрого CAT нормального диска. В результате она может выполнить CAT в стиле G+DOS, хотя на самом деле в этом нет необходимости.

Как бы то ни было, диагностировав ошибку и придумав исправление, я столкнулся с проблемой поиска 12 байт для необходимого патча. Что ж, мне пришлось пойти на крайние меры и распотрошить сообщения `SAVE...TO...` «Insert ORIG disc» и «Insert DEST disc», которые я и так уже сокращал ранее, чтобы вместить жизненно важный SNAPFIX!

Вместо двух отдельных сообщений теперь осталось только одно: «CHANGE disc» — в точности как на Disciple.

Я, конечно, рассуждаю как пользователь с двумя дисководами, но мне показалось, что оригинальные сообщения Source и Target в Betados все равно менее полезны, поскольку сообщения «LOADING...» и «SAVING...» сами по себе служат напоминанием о том, какой диск вставлять следующим. По крайней мере, я надеюсь, что именно так на это посмотрят владельцы одного дисковода!

Обнаружение этой ошибки и поиск дополнительной памяти, возможно, на самом деле были скрытым благом, поскольку за счет сокращения этих сообщений я выиграл достаточно места не только для устранения бага, но и для реализации `OPEN-3-OUT` — функции, которую я всегда хотел добавить в Betados, но до сих пор не видел возможности это сделать, так как для нее требуется 31 байт.

Тем не менее, это все равно было на грани: в запасе осталось всего 2 байта... Будем надеяться, что новых багов больше не будет!

Включение `OPEN-3-OUT`, по крайней мере, на мой взгляд, является важным обновлением для Betados, поскольку оно не только позволяет некоторым программам направлять вывод на принтер в файл, но также дает возможность работать таким утилитам, как OUT TO T (версия для +D).

Я назвал новую программу BETAFIX2 и добавил в нее также версию SNAPFIX для Betados, что упрощает дело, объединяя все в одной программе.

Еще одно последствие этого бага заключалось в том, что если ветвление все-таки уходило на выполнение CAT из G+DOS, процедура обновления системной переменной 124 пропускалась, оставляя ее значение неизменным и после завершения. Теперь это тоже исправлено.

С наилучшими пожеланиями,  
Miles

Меня заинтриговала заметка Malcolm Perry в Outlet 51 «Spreading the Muck». Однако Malcolm — или, скорее, его источник — немного запутался в принципах работы спутников GPS (Global Positioning System). Они не «зафиксированы в пространстве относительно Земли и относительно друг друга», а точность — не «1 км».

Если бы спутники были неподвижны в пространстве относительно Земли, они должны были бы находиться на геостационарной орбите и, следовательно, выстроились бы в прямую линию над экватором. Это сделало бы триангуляцию неоднозначной, поскольку любая позиция могла бы оказаться как к северу, так и к югу от экватора, а точность ухудшалась бы по мере продвижения на север — или на юг! В конце концов спутники просто скрылись бы за горизонтом. Точность определения высоты также была бы крайне низкой.

На самом деле около 20 спутников — так называемая группировка (созвездие) — находятся на орбитах, которые определенно не зафиксированы, и рассчитаны так, чтобы в любой момент времени в любой точке земной поверхности почти всегда были видны 4 спутника. Четыре спутника дают трехмерное определение координат, тогда как находясь на земле, можно обычно принять высоту за известную величину и обойтись двумерным позиционированием, для которого требуется всего три спутника.

Как же рассчитываются координаты? Каждый спутник непрерывно транслирует поток данных, содержащий его координаты и точное время отправки пакета. Если бы GPS-приемник имел свои собственные высокоточные атомные часы, он мог бы вычислить расстояние до спутника, определив время прохождения сигнала (на скорости света). Как нетрудно догадаться, из-за этого приемник стоил бы невероятно дорого, и его уж точно нельзя было бы положить в карман!

Итак, у вас есть координаты спутника и время, когда он находился в этой точке, что дает следующее уравнение:

```text
      d = ( Tr - Ts ) x c
```

где d — расстояние от приемника до спутника, Tr и Ts — время приемника и спутника, а c — скорость света. Tr неизвестно, поэтому d вычислить нельзя.

Однако одновременные данные с 4 спутников дают достаточно информации, чтобы рассчитать время приемника и, следовательно, получить трехмерную фиксацию. (Проще говоря, если вспомнить школьную математику, систему из четырех уравнений с четырьмя неизвестными можно решить). Если принять высоту за константу, то координаты можно вычислить по 3 спутникам.

В гражданском стандарте точность может достигать 20-30 метров, однако транслируемые спутниками данные намеренно загрубляются правительством США, чтобы сделать их непригодными для военных целей, что снижает точность примерно до 100 метров. Это называется «Selective Availability» (избирательная доступность), или SA. Вносимая ошибка непрерывно меняется.

Высокоточный зашифрованный сигнал доступен только американским военным. По иронии судьбы, во время войны в Персидском заливе в наличии были только обычные гражданские приемники, поэтому SA пришлось отключить!

Используя стационарный приемник (в пределах примерно 100 миль от вашего собственного приемника и, следовательно, принимающий данные от той же группы спутников — это важно), координаты которого точно известны, можно вычислить ошибку, вызванную SA, сравнив известные координаты с данными от системы GPS. При этом также компенсируются некоторые другие погрешности, вызванные искажениями пути прохождения сигнала в верхних слоях атмосферы.

Если передать эту информацию на мобильный приемник, то его координаты можно скорректировать, повысив точность до 1–3 метров. Эта система известна как дифференциальный GPS, или dGPS.

Поправки dGPS, транслируемые по каналам данных BBC (в зашифрованном виде), требуют оплаты ежегодной подписки, причем, как и упоминал Malcolm, стоимость зависит от выбранной точности.

Мое личное знакомство с GPS было связано с определением положения поезда, который автоматически записывал данные о состоянии путей во время движения по стране. Записанные данные затем можно было передавать по сотовой связи для анализа. Из других коммерческих сфер — использование рыболовными судами для поиска сетей и т.п.

Надеюсь, эта информация окажется полезной.
                  Gerry Bates.
